# Home Coffee Brewing

Brewing good coffee at home starts with the grind. A burr grinder produces a
consistent particle size, which matters more for flavor than almost any other
variable. Coarse grounds suit a French press, while a fine grind is needed
for espresso. Grinding too fine for a drip filter causes over-extraction and
a bitter cup.

Water temperature is the second lever. Most guides recommend somewhere
between 90 and 96 degrees Celsius. Water that is too cool under-extracts the
grounds and produces a sour, flat espresso or filter coffee. Water that is
too hot pulls out harsh, bitter compounds from the arabica or robusta beans.

The ratio of coffee to water also shapes the final cup. A common starting
point is one gram of ground coffee for every sixteen grams of water. From
that baseline, brewers adjust up or down depending on whether they prefer a
stronger or a more diluted espresso, pour-over, or French press.
